LESSON: REFLECTION AND CONGRUENCE

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: CORE MATHEMATICS
Strand: Measurements and Geometry
Topic 2.2: Reflection and Congruence
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 12

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reflection and Congruence, part of Measurements and Geometry in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 CORE MATHEMATICS.

Key inquiry question: How do we use reflection in day-to-day life? 2. Why do we use congruence in real life?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. work with peers to collect and observe different objects from the immediate environment and illustrate the lines and planes of symmetry. Learners with mobility difficulties could be supported to use appropriate mobility devices to move in the environment during this task. Those with manipulation difficulties could use appropriate assistive technology or be assisted by peers/learner support assistants to carry out the task,

2. use a plane mirror to locate the image of an object 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. work with peers to collect and observe different objects from the immediate environment and illustrate the lines and planes of symmetry. Learners with mobility difficulties could be supported to use appropriate mobility devices to move in the environment during this task. Those with manipulation difficulties could use appropriate assistive technology or be assisted by peers/learner support assistants to carry out the task,
2. use a plane mirror to locate the image of an object 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reflection and Congruence together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Learning to Learn: as the learner applies the properties of reflection to generate the image of an object on a given

mirror line.

● Creativity and Imagination: as the learner locates the image of an object placed at a point in front of a mirror.

28

Values:
● Responsibility: as the learner cautiously takes care of the mirror used in reflecting corresponding images.

● Respect: as the learner recognises the input of every member of the team as they work in groups to make paper

cutouts of different identical shapes to identify direct or opposite congruent shapes.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Road safety: as the learner discusses with peers the applications of reflections and congruence on images formed

by driving mirrors in enhancing road safety.

● Environment and Technology: as the learner selectively and cautiously collects and observes different objects from

the immediate environment and identifies the lines and planes of symmetry.

29

Suggested Learning Resources

Geometrical instruments (padded compass/ dividers, rulers with enhanced grip, protractor with handle), metre rule

with handle, charts on multiplication tables, paper cut-outs of regular shapes made of heavy gauge papers, drawing/

manila/ graph papers, scissors with enhanced grip, multipurpose communication boards on regular objects of different

shapes and sizes, white boards, slant boards, book holders, head pointers, page turners, pen/pencil holders, adapted

scientific calculators/ projectors, adhesives, positioning devices such as special seats with straps, adapted digital

devices such as adapted computers with larger screens
